Public-registry second review: both submitted artifacts are BENIGN.

85ed9652e88c126beec02d6c87055861f124a277f7edd403b51786fe72ff2a98
telemetry-helper 1.0.0, described as usage telemetry for install analytics.
Its only lifecycle hook runs bash scripts/postinstall.sh. The entire script
captures whoami, hostname, id, and uname -a; joins those outputs into MSG;
and sends MSG as Discord webhook message content with curl -s -X POST.
Mocked Bash functions confirmed the actual expanded curl argument vector.
No live identity utilities or network client were invoked in that trace.
There are no file reads, environment dumps, secret access, downloaded code,
persistence, elevation, or obfuscation. The endpoint has a sequential numeric
ID and alphabetic token; delivery is unverified. Host reporting is disclosed
by the package purpose. Neither the hook nor its host queries establishes
unauthorized activity. Retain one suspicious capability for the unusual
install-hook/profile/webhook combination, and notable underlying operations.
The new file-scoped composite requires an actual POST operation alongside
host queries and a webhook path. Its archive-level hook companion states
co-occurrence; it does not claim a verified path-to-script or source-to-body
binding. Split-member, endpoint-only and no-send controls exercise that limit.

8119150267de156614de8b7dcb54b2a3af3210f53398078b8a9b3cfbb0b36d5c
big-number-utils 1.0.0, claiming a pure-JavaScript big-number implementation
and the indutny/bn.js repository. The archive contains only package.json and
lib/entry.js. The main file synchronously invokes an anonymous function;
that function requires its declared next-runtimejs dependency for side
effects, defines an identity helper, and conditionally assigns module.exports.
The IIFE receives no argument, so its module parameter shadows the outer
CommonJS module with undefined and the assignment is unreachable. A QuickJS
context with a mocked require confirmed one import and unchanged exports.
A missing dependency throws directly; there is no fallback downloader.
Padding comments contain no encoded content or executable payload. The
artifact does not implement its advertised arithmetic API, but a broken or
misdescribed package is insufficient evidence of malware. The dependency's
bytes are absent and its version is a floating range: no behavior is attributed
to it. Repository mismatch, dependency declaration and side-effect require
remain neutral observations. No external reputation or scanner verdict was
used to establish behavior.

Both archive hashes were checked, and all regular members were compared
byte-for-byte with the supplied extraction. cleave facts was inspected for
each container and both executable members; no decoded payload was found.
The JavaScript flow analysis stops at the anonymous IIFE, so the complete
source and the mocked interpreter trace were used to resolve execution.

Corrections remove the unsupported next-runtimejs/name-based convictions,
retire the shell install-hook host-query hostility claims, and relocate the
postinstall local-shell declaration into lifecycle metadata. The obsolete
sh-word matcher also matched a .sh filename suffix; the existing interpreter
observation covers command context, and its consumer uses the precise local
script declaration. Exact version 1.0.0 plus a hook remains represented by
independent metadata instead of an objective. An unreferenced beacon.cjs
filename observation was consolidated into existing interpreter metadata to
keep lifecycle within its directory budget. The shell whoami observation
moved to process/user/query and became notable; its two exact consumers were
updated. Other JavaScript host-recon composites were outside this review.

The three original corpus fixtures, including the static-notification near
miss, now live under testdata/benign. Run:
  python3 testdata/install-telemetry-second-review/check.py

Full validation: removing the redundant exact-version/hook objective reduced
two benign corpus scores by one. Their exact score expectations were updated
(telemetry 17 to 16; application config 13 to 12), preserving the required
behavior traits and zero-hostile/zero-suspicious constraints.
